      <section class="report-section" id="report-methodology">
        <h3>12. Research methodology and experimental evaluation</h3>
        <p>The intended evaluation is a paired, controlled comparison of <code>Legacy_Static_TDMA</code> and <code>Tac-TAD</code>. The two scheduler arms must receive the same initial terrain, ACN route and motion, node positions, traffic configuration, RF/environment parameters, simulation duration, and random inputs where randomness is introduced. Only the scheduler policy should differ. A single browser session is useful for exploration, but comparative claims should be generated from recorded run manifests and repeatable worker runs.</p>
        <h4>12.1 Experimental procedure</h4>
        <ol>
          <li>Record the commit, runtime, host, scheduler policy, scenario, terrain asset/version, RF and weather parameters, trajectory, node inventory, traffic profile, duration, and seed or seed status.</li>
          <li>Warm up both arms using the same initialization rule, then run each for the same number of 20 ms frames. Keep the physical frame count separate from wall-clock execution time.</li>
          <li>Use paired scenarios: for each scenario identifier, run Static TDMA and Tac-TAD with identical inputs. Randomized scenario order may be used to reduce ordering effects, but the pairing must be retained.</li>
          <li>Export raw observations before aggregation. Keep failed, incomplete, and excluded runs with an explicit reason rather than silently removing them.</li>
          <li>Report results by scenario and in aggregate, with sample count, missing data, uncertainty, and the exact denominator for every percentage.</li>
        </ol>
        <h4>12.2 Primary and secondary metrics</h4>
        <table class="doc-table-clean"><thead><tr><th>Metric</th><th>Definition and purpose</th></tr></thead><tbody>
          <tr><td>Delivered goodput</td><td><code>totalBitsTransmitted</code> over the evaluation interval. This is payload dequeued while the link is usable, not theoretical PHY capacity.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Goodput distribution</td><td>Per-frame or defined-window throughput percentiles, such as P50 and P95, with the window and zero-value treatment stated.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Outage waste</td><td><code>totalBitsWastedOnOutage</code> and its explicitly defined denominator. This measures payload dequeued but not deliverable on an outage link.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Queue drops</td><td>Delay drops and overflow drops reported separately, both per-frame and cumulative. They must not be conflated with RF outage.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Backlog and delay</td><td>Total backlog bits plus packet sojourn/head-of-line delay by QoS class, including the relevant packet-delay budget.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Service and utilization</td><td>Scheduled uplink airtime, available airtime, unused/reclaimed airtime, allocation count, and utilization percentage.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>QoS protection</td><td>Class-specific delivery, delay, and drop outcomes for 5QI 69, 65, 67, and 70; aggregate goodput alone can hide tactical-priority regressions.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Execution performance</td><td>Worker step-time percentiles, wall-clock throughput, memory, and UI frame timing measured separately from simulated network outcomes.</td></tr>
        </tbody></table>
        <h4>12.3 Statistical evaluation plan</h4>
        <p>For each paired scenario, calculate the Tac-TAD minus Static difference (and the ratio only when the denominator is meaningful). Summarize paired differences with mean, median, standard deviation, interquartile range, and confidence intervals. Use a paired t-test only when the distribution and independence assumptions are defensible; otherwise use a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test or a permutation/bootstrap interval over scenario-level paired differences. Report effect sizes alongside p-values, correct for multiple primary comparisons when several hypotheses are tested, and treat confidence intervals crossing zero as inconclusive rather than as evidence of equivalence.</p>
        <p>Frames within one run are temporally correlated, so they must not be treated as independent experimental replicates. The recommended unit of inference is the paired scenario/run, with seeds or independently constructed scenarios as replicates. Pre-register primary metrics, exclusion rules, minimum run counts, and stopping criteria before inspecting comparative outcomes.</p>
        <div class="report-callout"><strong>Interpretation rule:</strong> an observed Tac-TAD improvement is a result for the specified model and scenario distribution. It is not evidence of universal scheduler superiority, field performance, or real-time operational suitability.</div>
      </section>

      <section class="report-section" id="report-standards">
        <h3>13. Industry standards and technical references</h3>
        <p>The following register records standards and standards-inspired references visible in the current implementation. A reference indicates the model’s intended engineering basis; it does not mean the project is certified, fully conformant, or a complete implementation of the publication.</p>
        <table class="doc-table-clean"><thead><tr><th>Reference</th><th>Use in this project</th><th>Implementation status</th></tr></thead><tbody>
          <tr><td>ITU-R P.834</td><td>Effective Earth-radius/refraction geometry, using the configured <code>k = 4/3</code> approximation.</td><td>Implemented approximation; not a dynamic refractivity model.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>ITU-R P.676</td><td>Clear-air gaseous attenuation coefficient used for the 8 GHz link model.</td><td>Implemented simplified coefficient; not a full spectral atmospheric calculation.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>ITU-R P.838-3</td><td>Rain specific attenuation form with horizontal-polarization coefficients and a configured rain-cell path cap.</td><td>Implemented simplified rain model for the configured frequency/assumptions.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>ITU-R P.526</td><td>Engineering basis for Fresnel clearance and knife-edge/dominant-obstacle diffraction language.</td><td>Project approximation; rounded-crest and terrain treatment are not a complete P.526 implementation.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>3GPP 5QI / MCX QoS concepts</td><td>Queue profiles use project-mapped 5QI labels 69 (C2), 65 (voice), 67 (video), and 70 (photo), with priority and packet-delay-budget fields.</td><td>Project traffic model inspired by these concepts; not a complete 3GPP QoS or MCX protocol stack.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>3GPP Release 17 NTN</td><td>Referenced with DVB-S2X in the discrete MODCOD naming and threshold abstraction.</td><td>Standards-inspired lookup table; no NTN waveform, protocol, satellite, or conformance implementation.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>DVB-S2X</td><td>Names and spectral-efficiency tiers in the eight-entry MODCOD table used for SNR-to-bitrate mapping.</td><td>Engineering abstraction; not a DVB-S2X modem or link-level implementation.</td></tr>
        </tbody></table>
        <p>Free-space path loss, Friis geometry, thermal noise, queueing, TDMA framing, and Tac-TAD are project-defined engineering components. They should not be described as separate industry-standard implementations unless a source mapping and validation evidence are added.</p>
      </section>

      <section class="report-section" id="report-appendix">
        <h3>Appendix A. Mathematical background and technical formulation</h3>
        <p>This appendix records the mathematical formulations used by the active TypeScript/WebWorker implementation. It is an engineering traceability document, not a claim that the project implements every referenced standard in full. Equations marked <strong>established</strong> are common engineering identities; equations marked <strong>standard-based approximation</strong> follow the project’s documented interpretation of a reference; equations marked <strong>project-defined</strong> or <strong>heuristic</strong> describe local implementation behavior.</p>
        <aside class="research-notice"><strong>Notation and units.</strong> Distances are in metres, time in seconds, frequency in hertz, speed in metres per second, power in dBm or watts as stated, and angles in radians unless degrees are explicitly shown. Every equation below has a unique appendix identifier and a source/function mapping.</aside>

        <h4>A.1 Radio propagation and link geometry</h4>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-1) &nbsp; d₂D = √(Δx² + Δy²), &nbsp;&nbsp; d₃D = √(Δx² + Δy² + Δz²)<br>         Δx = x<sub>A</sub> − x<sub>N</sub>, &nbsp; Δy = y<sub>A</sub> − y<sub>N</sub>, &nbsp; Δz = z<sub>A</sub> − z<sub>N</sub></div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>(xA,yA,zA)</code> is the ACN position in m MSL/local Cartesian coordinates; <code>(xN,yN,zN)</code> is the node position; <code>Δx,Δy,Δz</code> are component differences; <code>d2D</code> is horizontal range and <code>d3D</code> is slant range, all in m. <strong>Interpretation:</strong> this is the separation used by propagation delay and FSPL. <strong>Source:</strong> established Euclidean geometry; <code>TerrainEngine.computeSlantGeometry</code> in <code>src/core/terrain.ts</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> local Cartesian coordinates and endpoint heights are assumed; geodetic transformation and terrain datum errors are outside this equation.</p>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-2) &nbsp; τ<sub>prop</sub> = d₃D / c, &nbsp;&nbsp; τ<sub>TA</sub> = 2τ<sub>prop</sub> = 2d₃D / c</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>τprop</code> is one-way propagation delay in s; <code>τTA,geom</code> is the geometry-derived two-way timing value in s; <code>c</code> is the configured speed of light in m/s. <strong>Interpretation:</strong> the terrain geometry telemetry computes a two-way propagation relation. Scheduler allocation records currently use a separate fixed <code>timingAdvanceS = 0.001 s</code> field and do not consume <code>τTA,geom</code>. <strong>Source:</strong> established propagation identity; <code>computeSlantGeometry</code>, plus fixed allocation field in both scheduler implementations. <strong>Limits:</strong> neither value is a complete MAC timing-advance procedure; clock, synchronization, and waveform processing delay are not modeled.</p>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-3) &nbsp; φ = d₂D / R′<sub>e</sub>, &nbsp;&nbsp; e = atan2((R′<sub>e</sub> + z<sub>A</sub>)cosφ − (R′<sub>e</sub> + z<sub>N</sub>), (R′<sub>e</sub> + z<sub>A</sub>)sinφ)</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>R'e = kRe</code> is effective Earth radius in m; <code>φ</code> is central angle in rad; <code>e</code> is elevation angle, converted to degrees for telemetry. <strong>Interpretation:</strong> the implementation uses an effective-radius Earth geometry. <strong>Source:</strong> standard-based approximation associated with ITU-R P.834; <code>computeSlantGeometry</code> and <code>EnvironmentConfig.effectiveEarthRadiusM</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> <code>k = 4/3</code> is fixed by default; no measured refractivity profile is used.</p>

        <h4>A.2 Terrain obstruction, LOS/NLOS and Fresnel-zone analysis</h4>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-4) &nbsp; s = d₁ / D, &nbsp; (x(s),y(s),z<sub>LOS</sub>(s)) = (x<sub>N</sub>,y<sub>N</sub>,z<sub>N</sub>) + s(Δx,Δy,Δz)</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>D = d3D</code>; <code>d1</code> is distance from node to a sampled path point; <code>d2 = D − d1</code>; <code>s</code> is the path fraction; <code>zLOS</code> is linearly interpolated endpoint height. <strong>Interpretation:</strong> the terrain engine samples this ray at a configured interval, normally 100 m. <strong>Source:</strong> project-defined path sampling in <code>TerrainEngine.evaluateTerrainObstruction</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> finite sampling can miss sub-interval terrain features; out-of-coverage paths return invalid clearance rather than fabricated terrain.</p>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-5) &nbsp; h<sub>clear</sub>(d₁) = z<sub>LOS</sub>(d₁) − [h<sub>DEM</sub>(d₁) + b<sub>Earth</sub>(d₁,d₂)]<br>         b<sub>Earth</sub>(d₁,d₂) = d₁d₂ / (2R′<sub>e</sub>)</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>hDEM</code> is sampled terrain elevation in m; <code>bEarth</code> is effective-Earth bulge in m; <code>hclear</code> is clearance in m. <strong>Interpretation:</strong> positive clearance is above the effective terrain/curvature surface. <strong>Source:</strong> project implementation in <code>TerrainEngine.computeEarthBulge</code> and <code>evaluateTerrainObstruction</code>, with effective-radius basis from ITU-R P.834. <strong>Limits:</strong> the parabolic bulge is an approximation and is not a full spherical ray-trace or refractivity solution.</p>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-6) &nbsp; r₁(d₁,d₂) = √(λd₁d₂ / D), &nbsp;&nbsp; ρ = h<sub>clear</sub> / r₁</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>r1</code> is first Fresnel-zone radius in m; <code>λ = c/fc</code> is wavelength in m; <code>ρ</code> is normalized clearance. <strong>Interpretation:</strong> the engine retains the path sample with minimum normalized Fresnel clearance. <strong>Source:</strong> established Fresnel-zone relation; <code>evaluateTerrainObstruction</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> only the first-zone scalar clearance is used; antenna patterns, phase, multipath, and partial-zone field integration are not modeled.</p>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-7) &nbsp; LOS = (ρ ≥ 0.6) ∨ (0 &lt; ρ &lt; 0.6) with diffraction penalty; NLOS/outage geometry when ρ ≤ 0</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>ρ</code> is the minimum ratio in (A-6). <strong>Interpretation:</strong> the implementation preserves an <code>isLos</code> boolean for positive clearance, but assigns a nonzero diffraction loss when clearance is below 0.6 Fresnel radius; nonpositive clearance is treated as terrain obstruction. <strong>Source:</strong> project-defined threshold behavior in <code>evaluateTerrainObstruction</code> and <code>linkStatusClassifier.ts</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> the threshold is not presented as a universal LOS standard.</p>

        <h4>A.3 Knife-edge diffraction</h4>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-8) &nbsp; ν = −h<sub>clear</sub> √[(2/λ)(1/d₁ + 1/d₂)]</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>ν</code> is the dimensionless knife-edge parameter; for the obstructed branch <code>hclear ≤ 0</code>, so the implemented sign convention yields a nonnegative obstruction parameter. <strong>Source:</strong> established knife-edge diffraction form, implemented in <code>evaluateTerrainObstruction</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> sign conventions and the sampled dominant obstacle must not be generalized beyond this implementation.</p>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-9) &nbsp; L<sub>KE</sub> = 6.9 + 20log₁₀(√[(ν − 0.1)² + 1] + ν − 0.1)<br>         L<sub>diff</sub> = L<sub>KE</sub> + 12 dB</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>LKE</code> and <code>Ldiff</code> are losses in dB; the fixed 12 dB term is the project’s rounded-crest/Fock penalty. <strong>Source:</strong> knife-edge expression associated with ITU-R P.526; the added 12 dB term is project-defined in <code>evaluateTerrainObstruction</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> the project does not claim a complete P.526 implementation, multiple-edge diffraction, scattering, or validated rounded-crest calibration. The exact publication edition/equation mapping should be verified before formal citation.</p>

        <h4>A.4 Atmospheric attenuation and RF link budget</h4>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-10) &nbsp; FSPL = 20log₁₀(d₃D) + 20log₁₀(f<sub>c</sub>) + 20log₁₀(4π/c)</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>FSPL</code> is free-space path loss in dB; <code>d3D</code> is m; <code>fc</code> is Hz; <code>c</code> is m/s. <strong>Source:</strong> established Friis/free-space path-loss identity; <code>LinkBudgetEngine.computeFsplDb</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> isotropic/free-space assumptions do not include terrain, multipath, antenna pattern, or interference; terrain diffraction is added separately.</p>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-11) &nbsp; L<sub>gas</sub> = 0.012(d₃D / 1000) dB<br>         γ<sub>R</sub> = k<sub>H</sub>R<sup>αH</sup>, &nbsp; L<sub>rain</sub> = γ<sub>R</sub> min(d₃D/1000, ℓ<sub>rain</sub>)</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>Lgas</code> and <code>Lrain</code> are dB; <code>R</code> is rain rate in mm/h; <code>kH = 0.00411</code>, <code>αH = 1.39</code>; <code>ℓrain</code> is rain-cell length in km. <strong>Source:</strong> simplified ITU-R P.676/P.838-3-inspired terms in <code>computeGaseousAttenuationDb</code> and <code>computeRainAttenuationDb</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> the coefficient is fixed for the configured 8 GHz/horizontal-polarization assumption; no full frequency-, elevation-, or weather-profile integration is performed.</p>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-12) &nbsp; L<sub>total</sub> = L<sub>FSPL</sub> + L<sub>diff</sub> + L<sub>gas</sub> + L<sub>rain</sub> + L<sub>cable</sub> + M<sub>impl</sub><br>         P<sub>rx</sub> = P<sub>tx</sub> + G<sub>tx</sub> + G<sub>rx</sub> − L<sub>total</sub></div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> losses and margin are dB; <code>Ptx</code>/<code>Prx</code> are dBm; <code>Gtx</code>/<code>Grx</code> are dBi; <code>Lcable</code> and <code>Mimpl</code> are configured dB terms. <strong>Source:</strong> project link-budget summation in <code>LinkBudgetEngine.evaluateLink</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> the receiver gain is represented by the ACN gain field and the model does not resolve directional patterns or link asymmetry beyond configured node transmitter parameters.</p>

        <h4>A.5 Receiver noise, SNR and link adaptation</h4>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-13) &nbsp; P<sub>noise,W</sub> = k<sub>B</sub>T B 10<sup>NF/10</sup>, &nbsp;&nbsp; P<sub>noise,dBm</sub> = 10log₁₀(1000P<sub>noise,W</sub>)<br>         SNR<sub>dB</sub> = P<sub>rx,dBm</sub> − P<sub>noise,dBm</sub></div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>kB</code> is Boltzmann’s constant in J/K; <code>T</code> is temperature in K; <code>B</code> is bandwidth in Hz; <code>NF</code> is noise figure in dB; powers are W/dBm. <strong>Source:</strong> established thermal-noise relation and dBm conversion; <code>computeThermalNoiseFloorDbm</code> and <code>evaluateLink</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> constant temperature and scalar noise figure are assumed; interference and implementation-specific receiver effects are represented only by configured margin.</p>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-14) &nbsp; η(SNR) = η<sub>j</sub> for the highest threshold γ<sub>j</sub> ≤ SNR; &nbsp;&nbsp; R<sub>PHY</sub> = η(SNR)B</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>γj</code> is a MODCOD minimum-SNR threshold in dB; <code>ηj</code> is spectral efficiency in bit/s/Hz; <code>η</code> is selected efficiency; <code>RPHY</code> is nominal bitrate in bit/s. <strong>Source:</strong> threshold lookup and bitrate calculation in <code>selectModCod</code> and <code>evaluateLink</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> this is link adaptation by table lookup, not a waveform, coding, HARQ, or modem simulation.</p>

        <h4>A.6 MODCOD and PHY capacity</h4>
        <p>The current table contains eight named tiers from <code>pi/2-BPSK 1/3</code> at −1.5 dB and 0.33 bit/s/Hz through <code>64-APSK 5/6</code> at 22 dB and 4.95 bit/s/Hz. If no threshold is met, the table returns <code>LINK_OUTAGE</code>, zero spectral efficiency, and zero bitrate. These names are DVB-S2X / 3GPP Rel-17 NTN-inspired labels, not a claim of standards-compliant PHY behavior.</p>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-15) &nbsp; C<sub>slot</sub> = ⌊τ<sub>slot</sub>R<sub>PHY</sub>⌋ bits, &nbsp;&nbsp; B<sub>slot</sub> = ⌊C<sub>slot</sub>/8⌋ bytes</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>τslot</code> is scheduled payload duration in s; <code>Cslot</code> is integer slot capacity in bits; <code>Bslot</code> is dequeuing capacity in bytes. <strong>Source:</strong> <code>LegacyStaticScheduler.scheduleFrame</code> and <code>TacTadScheduler.scheduleFrame</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> PHY capacity is an upper bound for the slot; actual delivered application goodput depends on queued bytes, packet fit, outage state, and scheduler service.</p>

        <h4>A.7 TDMA framing and resource allocation</h4>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-16) &nbsp; T<sub>UL,avail</sub> = T<sub>frame</sub> − T<sub>ctrl</sub> − T<sub>DL</sub><br>         T<sub>frame</sub>=0.020 s, T<sub>ctrl</sub>=0.001 s, T<sub>DL</sub>∈{0.003,0.005} s</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> all terms are seconds; <code>TUL,avail</code> is available uplink time. <strong>Source:</strong> constants and scheduler arithmetic in <code>src/core/scheduler.ts</code>. <strong>Interpretation:</strong> the current rule selects 3 ms normally or 5 ms when downlink backlog exceeds 5,000 bytes; a 7 ms maximum constant exists but is not reached by the current rule. <strong>Limits:</strong> this is not a complete bidirectional MAC protocol.</p>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-17) &nbsp; τ<sub>static</sub> = [T<sub>UL,nominal</sub> − Nτ<sub>guard</sub>] / N</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>N</code> is registered node count; <code>τguard = 12 μs</code>; <code>TUL,nominal = 16 ms</code>; <code>τstatic</code> is equal payload slot duration. <strong>Source:</strong> <code>LegacyStaticScheduler.scheduleFrame</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> static service dequeues packets even when the link is unusable, which is intentionally measured as outage waste in this model.</p>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-18) &nbsp; T<sub>used</sub> = Σ<sub>i∈alloc</sub>(τ<sub>i</sub> + τ<sub>guard</sub>), &nbsp;&nbsp; U<sub>UL</sub> = 100 T<sub>used</sub>/T<sub>UL,avail</sub></div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>τi</code> is allocation duration; <code>Tused</code> is scheduled airtime including guards; <code>UUL</code> is utilization in percent. <strong>Source:</strong> both scheduler reports. <strong>Limits:</strong> utilization is airtime accounting, not application throughput or energy efficiency.</p>

        <h4>A.8 Traffic generation and queueing theory</h4>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-19) &nbsp; λ<sub>v</sub> = μ<sub>video,frame</sub>, &nbsp;&nbsp; K ~ Poisson(λ<sub>v</sub>)</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>λv</code> is configured mean video packets per frame; <code>K</code> is generated video packet count. <strong>Source:</strong> <code>GroundNodeTrafficSubsystem.poissonDraw</code> and <code>generateTraffic</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> C2, voice, and photo generation follow deterministic interval/window/remaining-bytes rules; the Poisson process is per frame and is not a calibrated field traffic model.</p>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-20) &nbsp; W<sub>p</sub>(t) = max(0,t − t<sub>arrival,p</sub>), &nbsp;&nbsp; t<sub>deadline,p</sub> = t<sub>arrival,p</sub> + PDB<sub>q</sub></div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>Wp</code> is packet sojourn time in s; <code>tarrival</code> and <code>tdeadline</code> are packet timestamps; <code>PDBq</code> is the QoS profile delay budget. <strong>Source:</strong> <code>Packet</code>, <code>enqueuePacket</code>, <code>getHolDelayS</code>, and queue pruning in <code>src/core/queues.ts</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> deadline pruning excludes 5QI 69 during the modeled shadow behavior; this is a project policy, not a universal QoS rule.</p>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-21) &nbsp; Q<sub>bits</sub>(t+) = Q<sub>bits</sub>(t) + A<sub>bits</sub>(t) − D<sub>bits</sub>(t) − X<sub>overflow,bits</sub>(t) − X<sub>expiry,bits</sub>(t)</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> all terms are bits; <code>Qbits</code> is queued backlog; <code>Abits</code> is admitted packet payload; <code>Dbits</code> is dequeued service; <code>Xoverflow,bits</code> and <code>Xexpiry,bits</code> are the sizes of evicted or expired packets. Separately, runtime counters <code>droppedOverflowCount</code> and <code>droppedDelayCount</code> count packets, not bits. <strong>Source:</strong> project-defined conservation summary of <code>FQCoDelQueue.enqueue</code>, <code>dequeue</code>, and <code>pruneExpiredPackets</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> the compact equation hides per-class ordering, packet-size fit, buffer ceilings, and eviction priority.</p>

        <h4>A.9 Tac-TAD and Static TDMA mathematical formulation</h4>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-22) &nbsp; Ψ<sub>i</sub> = Φ<sub>evac,i</sub> · U<sub>i</sub> · (R<sub>i</sub>/max(1000,R̄<sub>i</sub>)) · max[1, log₂(1 + Q<sub>i</sub>/8000)]<br>         U<sub>i</sub> = Σ<sub>q∈active</sub> w<sub>q</sub> exp(min(8, HOL<sub>i,q</sub>/PDB<sub>q</sub>))</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>Ψi</code> is Tac-TAD’s project-defined ranking score; <code>Φevac</code> is predictive evacuation/re-emergence boost; <code>Ui</code> is QoS urgency; <code>wq</code> is configured class weight; <code>HOL</code> is head-of-line age; <code>PDB</code> is delay budget; <code>Ri</code> is instantaneous bitrate; <code>R̄i</code> is the moving average; <code>Qi</code> is backlog bits. <strong>Source:</strong> exact structure in <code>TacTadScheduler.scheduleFrame</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> this is a deterministic heuristic composite, not a Lyapunov proof, trained policy, or optimization solution.</p>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-23) &nbsp; τ<sub>req,i</sub> = Q<sub>i</sub>/R<sub>i</sub>, &nbsp;&nbsp; τ<sub>i</sub> = min(τ<sub>req,i</sub>, τ<sub>max,normal</sub>, T<sub>remaining</sub> − τ<sub>guard</sub>)</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>τreq</code> is requested service duration; <code>τi</code> is normal Tac-TAD allocation; <code>τmax,normal</code> is the scheduler’s configured normal cap; <code>Tremaining</code> is remaining uplink time. <strong>Source:</strong> exact-fit sizing in <code>TacTadScheduler.scheduleFrame</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> a pre-occlusion flush changes the cap rule and can request at least the minimum slot; no global optimality or fairness guarantee follows.</p>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-24) &nbsp; Φ<sub>evac</sub> = 1 + 5[(3 − t<sub>occ</sub>)/3]<sub>0..1</sub> min(1,Q<sub>i</sub>/20000), &nbsp; PRE_OCCLUSION_FLUSH<br>         Φ<sub>evac</sub> = 4, &nbsp; RE_EMERGENCE_BURST</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>tocc</code> is predicted time to occlusion in s; <code>[·]0..1</code> denotes the implementation’s nonnegative/clamped ratio; backlog is in bits. <strong>Source:</strong> project heuristic in <code>TacTadScheduler.scheduleFrame</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> the warning horizon, factor 5, backlog scale, and re-emergence factor 4 are tuned constants; they require experimental sensitivity analysis.</p>

        <h4>A.10 Simulation timestep, state evolution and telemetry</h4>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-25) &nbsp; t<sub>n+1</sub> = t<sub>n</sub> + Δt, &nbsp;&nbsp; f<sub>n+1</sub> = f<sub>n</sub> + 1, &nbsp;&nbsp; Δt = 0.020 s = 1/50 s</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>tn</code> is simulated time; <code>fn</code> is frame index; <code>Δt</code> is the fixed physical timestep. <strong>Source:</strong> <code>SimulationWorkerManager.tickSimulation</code> and <code>FRAME_DT</code>. <strong>Interpretation:</strong> each tick refreshes obstruction state, generates/prunes traffic, runs both schedulers, accumulates metrics, and emits a telemetry frame. <strong>Limits:</strong> wall-clock timer interval and playback speed affect execution cadence only; they do not change <code>Δt</code>.</p>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-26) &nbsp; y<sub>n</sub> = {t<sub>n</sub>, f<sub>n</sub>, p<sub>ACN</sub>, v<sub>ACN</sub>, L<sub>i</sub>, Q<sub>i</sub>, S<sub>i</sub>, M<sub>n</sub>}</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>yn</code> is the published telemetry observation; <code>pACN/vACN</code> are position/velocity; <code>Li</code> is link state; <code>Qi</code> is queue state; <code>Si</code> is schedule/report state; <code>Mn</code> is accumulated metrics. <strong>Source:</strong> <code>buildTelemetryFrame</code>. <strong>Limits:</strong> telemetry is a snapshot at a worker frame boundary; it is not an event-sourced log of every internal operation.</p>

        <h4>A.11 Performance metrics and statistical evaluation</h4>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-27) &nbsp; G = Σ bits<sub>delivered</sub> / T<sub>eval</sub>, &nbsp;&nbsp; W<sub>outage</sub> = Σ bits<sub>dequeued,outage</sub><br>         B<sub>final</sub> = bits<sub>backlog at final frame</sub>, &nbsp;&nbsp; D<sub>drop</sub> = D<sub>delay</sub> + D<sub>overflow</sub></div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>G</code> is delivered goodput in bit/s; <code>Teval</code> is the stated evaluation interval; <code>Woutage</code> is outage-wasted payload bits; <code>Bfinal</code> is the final-frame backlog; <code>Ddrop</code> separates delay and overflow packet counts. <strong>Source:</strong> worker metric accumulation and <code>FrameScheduleReport</code>; <code>staticFinalBacklogBits</code> and <code>tacFinalBacklogBits</code> are overwritten each frame rather than accumulated. <strong>Limits:</strong> denominators and window boundaries must be reported; PHY capacity, scheduled service, dequeued payload, and delivered goodput are different quantities.</p>
        <div class="formula-card">(A-28) &nbsp; Δ<sub>j</sub> = m<sub>Tac,j</sub> − m<sub>Static,j</sub>, &nbsp;&nbsp; CI<sub>α</sub>(Δ̄) = Δ̄ ± t<sub>1−α/2,n−1</sub>s<sub>Δ</sub>/√n</div>
        <p><strong>Variables:</strong> <code>Δj</code> is a paired scenario difference; <code>m</code> is a metric; <code>n</code> is the number of independent paired scenario/run replicates; <code>sΔ</code> is the sample standard deviation; <code>CIα</code> is a confidence interval when the paired-t assumptions are reasonable. <strong>Source:</strong> project evaluation formulation described in the methodology section, not runtime code. <strong>Limits:</strong> use paired Wilcoxon or bootstrap/permutation alternatives when assumptions fail; do not treat correlated frames as independent replicates.</p>

        <h4>A.12 Model assumptions, approximations and limitations</h4>
        <table class="doc-table-clean"><thead><tr><th>Model area</th><th>Current assumption</th><th>Consequence</th><th>Source / status</th></tr></thead><tbody>
          <tr><td>Coordinates</td><td>Local Cartesian X east, Y north, Z MSL/elevation.</td><td>Projection and datum errors are not propagated as uncertainty.</td><td><code>terrain.ts</code>; implemented project coordinate model.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Terrain</td><td>DEM samples plus effective Earth bulge and configured geometric obstacles.</td><td>Resolution, sampling interval, and coverage boundaries limit obstruction fidelity.</td><td><code>evaluateTerrainObstruction</code>; project approximation.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Propagation</td><td>FSPL, scalar gas/rain loss, dominant-obstacle diffraction, scalar noise.</td><td>No multipath, scattering, interference, antenna pattern, or measured channel calibration.</td><td><code>linkBudget.ts</code>, <code>terrain.ts</code>.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Adaptation</td><td>Discrete SNR threshold table maps directly to spectral efficiency.</td><td>No modem, coding, HARQ, packet error probability, or waveform timing model.</td><td><code>MODCOD_TABLE</code>; standards-inspired abstraction.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Scheduling</td><td>Static equal slots versus deterministic Tac-TAD heuristic.</td><td>No proof of optimality, universal fairness, or learned policy behavior.</td><td><code>scheduler.ts</code>; project-defined.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Replay</td><td>Rolling telemetry snapshots.</td><td>Historical scrubbing is not deterministic re-execution.</td><td><code>simulationHistory.ts</code> and coordinators.</td></tr>
        </tbody></table>
        <p><strong>Reference verification status:</strong> the implementation comments and project report identify ITU-R P.526, P.676, P.834, P.838-3, 3GPP 5QI/MCX concepts, 3GPP Release 17 NTN, and DVB-S2X as engineering references. The exact editions, clause numbers, and publication equation numbers have not been independently verified in this appendix; they should be checked against the official publications before a formal academic or compliance citation is issued. No claim of full ITU-R, 3GPP, or DVB-S2X compliance is made.</p>
      </section>

      <section class="report-section" id="report-verification">
        <h3>14. Testing and verification</h3>
        <p>Verification is executable and source-based, not a substitute for field validation. The repository’s <code>npm test</code> command runs structural checks, typecheck, physics, scheduler, worker-state, trajectory, obstacle, historical, link-classification, Three.js foundation, geodesy, visualization, bandwidth, and integration checks. <code>npm run build</code> verifies the Vite production bundle; <code>git diff --check</code> checks patch whitespace.</p>
        <table class="doc-table-clean"><thead><tr><th>Evidence area</th><th>Current coverage</th></tr></thead><tbody>
          <tr><td>Trajectory</td><td>Ellipse compatibility, closed waypoint looping, speed/velocity continuity, geometry, and editor behavior.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>RF and geometry</td><td>Link budget terms, bandwidth validation, geodesy, DEM mapping, coverage, hillshade bounds, and cursor readout.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Scheduling and traffic</td><td>Scheduler invariants, worker state, historical scheduler, queues, link classification, goodput and data communication.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Visualization</td><td>Terrain canvas, path-profile/top-view, node inventory, Three.js foundation/terrain/entities, and integration hardening.</td></tr>
        </tbody></table>
        <p>Passing automated checks demonstrates implementation invariants for the tested cases. It does not establish real-world RF accuracy, operational readiness, or statistical superiority across scenarios.</p>
      </section>

      <section class="report-section" id="report-limitations">
        <h3>15. Limitations and future research</h3>
        <h4>Implemented capabilities</h4>
        <ul><li>Browser TypeScript worker simulation at a 20 ms physical step.</li><li>Terrain-aware LOS/Fresnel/diffraction screening, configurable rain and gas terms, adaptive MODCOD abstraction, QoS queues, two TDMA policies, trajectory editing, obstacle geometry, map views, and telemetry history.</li></ul>
        <h4>Simplifications and unresolved validation</h4>
        <ul>
          <li>No measured field telemetry synchronization or calibrated end-to-end channel model is present.</li>
          <li>Terrain diffraction uses bounded geometric approximations; multipath, scattering, antenna patterns, interference, and polarization effects are not simulated.</li>
          <li>The MODCOD table is a discrete engineering abstraction and is not proof of DVB-S2X or 3GPP conformance.</li>
          <li>History stores telemetry snapshots and does not provide deterministic re-execution from a complete event log.</li>
          <li>Legacy Python artifacts and archived benchmark numbers are not current TypeScript results unless parity is independently demonstrated.</li>
        </ul>
        <div class="report-callout report-callout-warning"><strong>Historical benchmark results (legacy Python engine):</strong> archived values are not a verified statement about the current TypeScript engine and must not be presented as current-worker measurements without a controlled <strong>Python ↔ TypeScript parity</strong> study. <strong>Data-quality flag:</strong> archived distributions require review before use in claims.</div>
        <h4>Recommended research extensions</h4>
        <ol><li>Calibrate propagation and antenna assumptions against measured link data.</li><li>Define cross-engine golden fixtures only where legacy parity is required.</li><li>Run paired multi-seed experiments with manifests, confidence intervals, and metric definitions.</li><li>Profile worker latency, UI frame time, memory, and long-duration stability on named hardware.</li><li>Extend the channel model with interference, weather profiles, and richer terrain/multipath treatment.</li></ol>
      </section>

      <footer class="research-footer">Document status: current implementation reference. Source files are authoritative; numerical claims require reproducible run provenance and should not be read as field-performance guarantees.</footer>
    </div>
  </section>

  </section>
</main>

<script>
/* Render-quality layer */
(function(){
  const gc=HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext;
  HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext=function(t,...a){const c=gc.call(this,t,...a);if(c&&t==='2d'){c.imageSmoothingQuality='high';c.lineJoin='round'}return c};
})();

/* UX layer: quick tour, expert view, keyboard shortcuts. */
(function(){
  const $=id=>document.getElementById(id), KEY='xband-tour-dismissed';
  const welcome=$('welcome'); let seen=false;
  try{seen=localStorage.getItem(KEY)==='1'}catch(_){}
  if(welcome) welcome.hidden=seen;
  $('welcome-dismiss')?.addEventListener('click',()=>{welcome.hidden=true;try{localStorage.setItem(KEY,'1')}catch(_){}});
  $('btn-help')?.addEventListener('click',()=>{window.switchMainTab('tab-overview');welcome.hidden=false;welcome.scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'})});
  const ex=$('btn-expert');
  ex?.addEventListener('click',()=>{const on=ex.classList.toggle('active');ex.setAttribute('aria-pressed',String(on));document.querySelectorAll('details[data-adv]').forEach(d=>d.open=on)});
  const tabs=['overview','scheduler','network','terrain','terminal','doc'];
  document.addEventListener('keydown',e=>{
    if(e.ctrlKey||e.metaKey||e.altKey) return;
    if(e.key==='Escape') return window.closeUploadModal&&window.closeUploadModal();
    if(e.target.closest&&e.target.closest('input,select,textarea,button,[contenteditable]')) return;
    if(/^[1-6]$/.test(e.key)) window.switchMainTab('tab-'+tabs[e.key-1]);
    else if(e.key===' '){e.preventDefault();window.togglePause()}
    else if(e.key==='.') window.stepSim();
  });
})();
</script>

function networkCanvasContext(id) {
  const canvas = $(id);
  if (!canvas) return null;
  const rect = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
  const ratio = Math.max(1, window.devicePixelRatio || 1);
  const width = Math.max(280, Math.round(rect.width || canvas.parentElement?.clientWidth || 640));
  const height = Math.max(220, Math.round(rect.height || 360));
  if (canvas.width !== width * ratio || canvas.height !== height * ratio) {
    canvas.width = width * ratio;
    canvas.height = height * ratio;
  }
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
  if (!ctx) return null;
  ctx.setTransform(ratio, 0, 0, ratio, 0, 0);
  return { ctx, width, height };
}

function networkDrawMetric(ctx, values, label, unit, colorFor, yOffset, height, width, minOverride = null, maxOverride = null) {
  const left = 68, right = 16, top = yOffset + 22, bottom = yOffset + height - 14;
  const plotWidth = Math.max(20, width - left - right);
  const finiteValues = values.flatMap(item => item.values.filter(Number.isFinite));
  let min = minOverride ?? (finiteValues.length ? Math.min(...finiteValues) : 0);
  let max = maxOverride ?? (finiteValues.length ? Math.max(...finiteValues) : 1);
  if (max <= min) { const pad = Math.max(1, Math.abs(max) * 0.05); min -= pad; max += pad; }

  if (yOffset > 0) {
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#1a2430';
    ctx.lineWidth = 1;
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.moveTo(left, yOffset);
    ctx.lineTo(width - right, yOffset);
    ctx.stroke();
  }

  ctx.fillStyle = '#94a3b8';
  ctx.font = '600 11px system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif';
  ctx.fillText(label, 6, yOffset + 13);

  ctx.fillStyle = '#64748b';
  ctx.font = '10px "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, monospace';
  ctx.fillText(`${max.toFixed(1)} ${unit}`, 6, top + 3);
  ctx.fillText(`${min.toFixed(1)} ${unit}`, 6, bottom + 1);

  ctx.strokeStyle = '#1e293b';
  ctx.lineWidth = 1;
  ctx.beginPath();
  ctx.moveTo(left, top);
  ctx.lineTo(width - right, top);
  ctx.lineTo(width - right, bottom);
  ctx.lineTo(left, bottom);
  ctx.closePath();
  ctx.stroke();

  const mid = (top + bottom) / 2;
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#16202c';
  ctx.setLineDash([3, 4]);
  ctx.beginPath();
  ctx.moveTo(left, mid);
  ctx.lineTo(width - right, mid);
  ctx.stroke();
  ctx.setLineDash([]);

  for (const series of values) {
    ctx.strokeStyle = colorFor(series.key);
    ctx.lineWidth = 2;
    ctx.beginPath();
    let started = false;
    series.values.forEach((value, index) => {
      if (!Number.isFinite(value)) { started = false; return; }
      const x = left + (series.values.length <= 1 ? 0 : (index / (series.values.length - 1)) * plotWidth);
      const y = bottom - ((value - min) / (max - min)) * (bottom - top);
      if (!started) ctx.moveTo(x, y); else ctx.lineTo(x, y);
      started = true;
    });
    ctx.stroke();
  }
}

function networkVisibleSamples() {
  const samples = networkPerformanceHistory.getSamples();
  const range = Number($('network-time-range')?.value || 30);
  const newest = samples.length ? samples[samples.length - 1].simulationTimeS : 0;
  return samples.filter(sample => sample.simulationTimeS >= newest - range);
}

function drawNetworkCharts() {
  const samples = networkVisibleSamples();
  const selected = new Set(Array.from($('network-node-select')?.selectedOptions || []).map(option => Number(option.value)));
  const individualCard = $('network-individual-card');
  const aggregateCard = $('network-aggregate-card');
  const mode = $('network-view-mode')?.value || 'individual';
  if (individualCard) individualCard.style.display = mode === 'individual' ? '' : 'none';
  if (aggregateCard) aggregateCard.style.display = mode === 'aggregate' ? '' : 'none';
  const empty = $('network-dashboard-empty');
  if (empty) empty.textContent = samples.length && selected.size ? `${selected.size} node${selected.size === 1 ? '' : 's'} selected · ${samples.length} samples` : 'Select one or more ground nodes to compare performance.';

  const individualCanvas = networkCanvasContext('network-individual-chart');
  if (individualCanvas && mode === 'individual') {
    const ids = [...selected];
    const colors = ['#38bdf8', '#10b981', '#f59e0b', '#f472b6', '#a78bfa', '#fb923c'];
    const make = key => ids.map((id, index) => ({
      key: id,
      values: samples.map(sample => {
        const node = sample.nodes.find(item => item.nodeId === id);
        if (!node) return NaN;
        if (key === 'snr') return node.linkValid ? (node.snrDb ?? NaN) : NaN;
        if (key === 'rate') return node.rateMbps;
        return node.transferredMb;
      }),
    }));
    individualCanvas.ctx.clearRect(0, 0, individualCanvas.width, individualCanvas.height);
    individualCanvas.ctx.fillStyle = '#0b1015'; individualCanvas.ctx.fillRect(0, 0, individualCanvas.width, individualCanvas.height);
    const enabled = [
      [$('network-show-snr')?.checked, 'snr', 'SNR', 'dB'],
      [$('network-show-rate')?.checked, 'rate', 'Rate', 'Mbps'],
      [$('network-show-transferred')?.checked, 'transferred', 'Transferred', 'MB'],
    ].filter(item => item[0]);
    const rowHeight = enabled.length ? individualCanvas.height / enabled.length : individualCanvas.height;
    enabled.forEach((item, index) => networkDrawMetric(individualCanvas.ctx, make(item[1]), item[2], item[3], id => colors[ids.indexOf(id) % colors.length], index * rowHeight, rowHeight, individualCanvas.width));
    const legend = ids.map((id, index) => `${networkNodeNames.get(id) || `Node ${id}`} (${colors[index % colors.length]})`).join(' · ');
    setText('network-individual-value', legend || 'No nodes selected');
  }

  const aggregateCanvas = networkCanvasContext('network-aggregate-chart');
  if (aggregateCanvas && mode === 'aggregate') {
    const aggregates = samples.map(aggregateNetworkSample);
    aggregateCanvas.ctx.clearRect(0, 0, aggregateCanvas.width, aggregateCanvas.height);
    aggregateCanvas.ctx.fillStyle = '#0b1015'; aggregateCanvas.ctx.fillRect(0, 0, aggregateCanvas.width, aggregateCanvas.height);
    const enabled = [
      [$('network-show-snr')?.checked, 'snr', 'SNR avg / min', 'dB'],
      [$('network-show-rate')?.checked, 'rate', 'Total rate', 'Mbps'],
      [$('network-show-transferred')?.checked, 'transferred', 'Total transferred', 'MB'],
    ].filter(item => item[0]);
    const rowHeight = enabled.length ? aggregateCanvas.height / enabled.length : aggregateCanvas.height;
    enabled.forEach((item, index) => {
      const series = item[1] === 'snr'
        ? [{ key: 'avg', values: aggregates.map(value => value.averageSnrDb ?? NaN) }, { key: 'min', values: aggregates.map(value => value.minimumSnrDb ?? NaN) }]
        : [{ key: item[1], values: aggregates.map(value => item[1] === 'rate' ? value.totalRateMbps : value.totalTransferredMb) }];
      networkDrawMetric(aggregateCanvas.ctx, series, item[2], item[3], key => key === 'min' ? '#ef4444' : '#38bdf8', index * rowHeight, rowHeight, aggregateCanvas.width);
    });
    const last = aggregates[aggregates.length - 1];
    setText('network-aggregate-value', last ? `${last.validLinkCount} valid links · ${last.totalRateMbps.toFixed(2)} Mbps` : 'No network samples');
  }
}

function updateNetworkNodeOptions(nodes) {
  const select = $('network-node-select');
  if (!select) return;
  const signature = nodes.map(node => `${node.node_id}:${node.name || ''}:${node.link_outage === false ? 'up' : 'down'}`).join('|');
  if (signature === networkNodeOptionsSignature) return;
  networkNodeOptionsSignature = signature;
  const selected = new Set(Array.from(select.selectedOptions).map(option => Number(option.value)));
  const ids = nodes.map(node => node.node_id);
  select.replaceChildren(...nodes.map(node => {
    networkNodeNames.set(node.node_id, node.name || `Node ${node.node_id}`);
    const option = document.createElement('option');
    option.value = String(node.node_id);
    option.textContent = `${node.name || `Node ${node.node_id}`} · ${node.link_outage === false ? 'connected' : 'disconnected'}`;
    option.selected = selected.size ? selected.has(node.node_id) : ids.indexOf(node.node_id) < 3;
    return option;
  }));
  const urlParams = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
  if (urlParams.has('node') && selectedNodeId === -1) {
    const nid = Number(urlParams.get('node'));
    if (nodes.some(n => n.node_id === nid)) {
      handleNodeSelection(nid);
    }
  }
}

function ingestNetworkPerformance(frame) {
  const nodes = Array.isArray(frame?.nodes_telemetry) ? frame.nodes_telemetry : [];
  updateNetworkNodeOptions(nodes);
  const sample = networkPerformanceHistory.ingest({
    frameIndex: Number(frame?.frame_index ?? 0),
    simulationTimeS: Number(frame?.sim_time_s ?? 0),
    nodes,
  }, networkGraphUpdatesEnabled);
  if (sample && (sample.simulationTimeS - networkLastRenderTime >= 0.1 || document.visibilityState !== 'visible')) {
    networkLastRenderTime = sample.simulationTimeS;
    drawNetworkCharts();
  }
}

function setupNetworkDashboard() {
  ['network-view-mode', 'network-node-select', 'network-time-range', 'network-show-snr', 'network-show-rate', 'network-show-transferred'].forEach(id => {
    $(id)?.addEventListener('change', drawNetworkCharts);
  });
  $('network-pause')?.addEventListener('click', () => {
    networkGraphUpdatesEnabled = !networkGraphUpdatesEnabled;
    const button = $('network-pause');
    if (button) button.textContent = networkGraphUpdatesEnabled ? 'Pause graph updates' : 'Resume graph updates';
    setText('network-dashboard-state', networkGraphUpdatesEnabled ? 'LIVE' : 'PAUSED');
    drawNetworkCharts();
  });
  $('network-clear')?.addEventListener('click', () => {
    networkPerformanceHistory.clear();
    networkLastRenderTime = 0;
    drawNetworkCharts();
  });
  window.addEventListener('resize', drawNetworkCharts);
}
function updateStepControlUI(enabled) {
  const btn = $('btn-step');
  if (!btn) return;
  btn.disabled = !enabled;
  btn.classList.toggle('disabled', !enabled);
  if (!enabled) {
    btn.setAttribute('aria-disabled', 'true');
    btn.title = 'Stepped cycle in progress...';
  } else {
    btn.removeAttribute('aria-disabled');
    btn.title = 'Advance one 20 ms frame (.)';
  }
}

function updatePauseButtonUI() {
  const btn = $('btn-pause');
  if (!btn) return;
  const pbMode = dataCommVisualizer.getPlaybackMode();
  const stepState = dataCommVisualizer.getSteppedLifecycle();
  const visualPaused = dataCommVisualizer.isVisualPaused();

  if (pbMode === 'stepped') {
    if (stepState === 'playing') {
      btn.textContent = visualPaused ? 'RESUME' : 'PAUSE';
      btn.classList.toggle('active', visualPaused);
      btn.title = visualPaused ? 'Resume stepped visual playback (Space)' : 'Pause stepped visual playback (Space)';
    } else if (stepState === 'complete') {
      btn.textContent = 'RESUME SIM';
      btn.classList.add('active');
      btn.title = 'Resume continuous simulation (Space)';
    } else {
      btn.textContent = isPaused ? 'RESUME' : 'PAUSE';
      btn.classList.toggle('active', isPaused);
      btn.title = 'Pause or resume (Space)';
    }
  } else {
    btn.textContent = isPaused ? 'RESUME' : 'PAUSE';
    btn.classList.toggle('active', isPaused);
    btn.title = 'Pause or resume (Space)';
  }
}

dataCommVisualizer.setOnSteppedCycleComplete(() => {
  updateStepControlUI(true);
  updatePauseButtonUI();
});

// User-adjustable map/detail split, persisted independently.
(function setupWorkspaceResizing() {
  const workspace = $('main-workspace');
  const handle = $('map-resize-handle');
  if (!workspace || !handle) return;
  const clamp = (n, min, max) => Math.max(min, Math.min(max, n));
  let saved = 44;
  try { saved = Number(localStorage.getItem('xband-map-width-pct')) || 44; } catch (_) {}
  workspace.style.setProperty('--map-width', `${clamp(saved, 28, 72)}%`);
  let dragStartX = 0, dragStartPct = 44, dragging = false;
  const setWidth = pct => {
    const bounds = workspace.getBoundingClientRect();
    const minPct = Math.max(260 / Math.max(bounds.width, 1) * 100, 24);
    const maxPct = Math.min(76, 100 - 340 / Math.max(bounds.width, 1) * 100);
    const next = clamp(pct, minPct, maxPct);
    workspace.style.setProperty('--map-width', `${next}%`);
    handle.setAttribute('aria-valuenow', String(Math.round(next)));
    try { localStorage.setItem('xband-map-width-pct', String(next)); } catch (_) {}
    requestAnimationFrame(resizeCanvases);
  };
  handle.addEventListener('pointerdown', event => {
    if (event.button !== 0) return;
    dragging = true; dragStartX = event.clientX;
    const mapWidth = $('persistent-map-panel').getBoundingClientRect().width;
    dragStartPct = mapWidth / workspace.getBoundingClientRect().width * 100;
    handle.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId);
    document.body.classList.add('is-resizing');
    event.preventDefault();
  });
  handle.addEventListener('pointermove', event => {
    if (!dragging) return;
    const width = workspace.getBoundingClientRect().width;
    setWidth(dragStartPct + (event.clientX - dragStartX) / width * 100);
  });
  const stop = () => { dragging = false; document.body.classList.remove('is-resizing'); };
  handle.addEventListener('pointerup', stop);
  handle.addEventListener('pointercancel', stop);
  handle.addEventListener('keydown', event => {
    const current = $('persistent-map-panel').getBoundingClientRect().width / workspace.getBoundingClientRect().width * 100;
    if (event.key === 'ArrowLeft') { setWidth(current - 2); event.preventDefault(); }
    if (event.key === 'ArrowRight') { setWidth(current + 2); event.preventDefault(); }
    if (event.key === 'Home') { setWidth(30); event.preventDefault(); }
    if (event.key === 'End') { setWidth(70); event.preventDefault(); }
  });
  window.addEventListener('resize', () => requestAnimationFrame(resizeCanvases));
  document.querySelectorAll('.scheduler-layout > *, .terrain-layout > *, .terrain-grid > *, .terminal-layout > *, .doc-layout > .report-section').forEach(panel => {
    panel.classList.add('resizable-panel', 'is-vert-resizable');
  });
})();
